acceptedAnswer.text: A synthetic alpha-MSH analog, commonly described in the literature as [Nle4, D-Phe7]-alpha-MSH, studied for its interaction with the melanocortin 1 receptor and its role in pigmentation research.

mainEntity.name: Is Melanotan 1 the same as Melanotan II?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. They are structurally distinct alpha-MSH-derived analogs — MT-I is linear, MT-II is cyclic — with different reported receptor activity and different research histories.

mainEntity.name: Is Melanotan 1 the same as afamelanotide?

acceptedAnswer.text: They share the same core chemical structure. Afamelanotide specifically refers to the regulated pharmaceutical product; it is not a synonym for commercial research-market material sold as Melanotan 1.
The melanocortin 1 receptor — a receptor expressed primarily on skin melanocytes that, when activated, drives the principal pigmentation signaling pathway in human skin.

mainEntity.name: What does "Spray" mean for this research material?

acceptedAnswer.text: It describes the packaging and delivery mechanism. It does not, by itself, indicate a route of administration, and no route is specified or assumed.

mainEntity.name: Does this page provide a human dosage?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Dosage and administration information is outside the scope of this Research Use Only page and is not provided.
Research Use Only — the material is intended exclusively for laboratory research and is not intended for human or veterinary use.
